answer: Drift-keyed burst shaping: each agent derives a public send-window and packet-size schedule from its quartz oscillator’s measured frequency offset plus a rotating cipher. Traffic must trace a hollow envelope—periodic silent gaps and shaped microbursts—matching that schedule. Validators score multi-hour drift consistency; cloned schedules correlate and fail. Sybils need distinct physical timing sources, continuous padded bandwidth, and long observation/upkeep, so N identities cost roughly N real oscillators plus N-times traffic overhead.
